title: Module objects and the category $\Mod_{\Lambda_X}$
statement:
Let $(\mathcal C,\otimes,\mathbf 1)$ be a monoidal category with associator $\alpha$ and
left unitor $\lambda$. Let $\mathcal R$ be a monoid object of $\mathcal C$, with
multiplication $\mu\colon\mathcal R\otimes\mathcal R\to\mathcal R$ and unit
$\eta\colon\mathbf 1\to\mathcal R$. When $\mathcal C$ is a category of abelian sheaves with
its tensor product, these are the ring objects of [sk-def-sfb-ring-object].

1. A *(left) $\mathcal R$-module object* is an object $M$ of $\mathcal C$ with an
   *action* $\gamma_M\colon\mathcal R\otimes M\to M$ that is unital and associative:
   $$
   \gamma_M\circ(\eta\otimes M)=\lambda_M,\qquad
   \gamma_M\circ(\mu\otimes M)=\gamma_M\circ(\mathcal R\otimes\gamma_M)\circ\alpha_{\mathcal R,\mathcal R,M}.
   $$
2. A *morphism of $\mathcal R$-module objects* $f\colon M\to N$ is a morphism of
   $\mathcal C$ with $f\circ\gamma_M=\gamma_N\circ(\mathcal R\otimes f)$. With the
   composition of $\mathcal C$, the $\mathcal R$-module objects form a category
   $\Mod_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal C)$. It has a forgetful functor
   $\Mod_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal C)\to\mathcal C$, $(M,\gamma_M)\mapsto M$. The *regular
   module* is $\mathcal R$ itself with action $\mu$.
3. Let $X$ be a scheme with small pro-étale site $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$
   ([def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]). Give $\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)$ the tensor product of
   [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]. Let $\Lambda$ be a condensed ring and let
   $\Lambda_X=p_X^*\Lambda$ be its pullback, a ring object of $\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)$
   ([sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]). The category of *sheaves of
   $\Lambda_X$-modules* is
   $$
   \Mod_{\Lambda_X}:=\Mod_{\Lambda_X}\bigl(\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)\bigr).
   $$

proof.text: For the identity, $\mathrm{id}_M\circ\gamma_M=\gamma_M=\gamma_M\circ(\mathcal R\otimes\mathrm{id}_M)$ by functoriality of $\mathcal R\otimes-$. If $f\colon M\to N$ and $g\colon N\to P$ commute with the actions, then $g\circ f\circ\gamma_M=g\circ\gamma_N\circ(\mathcal R\otimes f)=\gamma_P\circ(\mathcal R\otimes g)\circ(\mathcal R\otimes f)=\gamma_P\circ(\mathcal R\otimes(g\circ f))$. Thus identities and composites are module morphisms. Their category laws are the corresponding laws in $\mathcal C$. Forgetting the action preserves these identities and composites by definition, hence gives the claimed functor.

source.place: first three sentences: identity and composite calculation; category and forgetful functor

proof.text: For $M=\mathcal R$ and $\gamma_M=\mu$, the two module axioms become $\mu\circ(\eta\otimes\mathcal R)=\lambda_{\mathcal R}$ and $\mu\circ(\mu\otimes\mathcal R)=\mu\circ(\mathcal R\otimes\mu)\circ\alpha_{\mathcal R,\mathcal R,\mathcal R}$. These are exactly the left unit and associativity laws of the given monoid object, as stated in [sk-def-sfb-ring-object]. Hence $(\mathcal R,\mu)$ is the regular module.

source.place: For the regular module: the displayed left unit and associativity laws

proof.text: For the scheme $X$ of part 3, [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor] supplies the monoidal structure on $\mathcal C=\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)$, with sheafified objectwise $\otimes_{\mathbf Z}$ and unit $\underline{\mathbf Z}$. The statement of [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] supplies the ring object $\mathcal R=\Lambda_X=p_X^*\Lambda$ in this very category. Therefore the objects and morphisms defined in parts 1 and 2 specialize to abelian sheaves with an action $\Lambda_X\otimes M\to M$ satisfying precisely the displayed unit and associativity equations. Step 1 supplies their category and forgetful functor, and step 2 supplies its regular module $\Lambda_X$. This defines the category $\Mod_{\Lambda_X}$ in part 3.

source.place: last sentence: specialize to Lambda_X using its pulled-back ring-object structure
